# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book documents Stage 3 of the Computational Language Technologies project at HSLU, building on the data pipeline, exploratory analysis, and embeddings from Stages 1 and 2.

## Dataset

The AI Media Dataset (Kaggle) consists of 16,317 news articles covering artificial intelligence topics, collected between September 2024 and August 2025.

## Stage 3 Overview

Stage 3 implements a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system over the AI Media Dataset, integrating structured knowledge graphs with unstructured text retrieval:

- **Part I – Q&A Dataset:** Construction of 215 reviewed Q&A pairs from 80 representative passages, categorised into factual, analytical, and comparative types.
- **Part II – RAG Baseline:** Text-only RAG pipeline (Config A) using dense retrieval with ChromaDB.
- **Part III – Graph-Augmented RAG:** Entity-anchored retrieval integrating the provided knowledge graph (Config B) and our Stage 1 knowledge graph (Config C).
- **Part IV – Evaluation:** Custom LLM-judge and RAGAS-based comparison of all three configurations across faithfulness, answer relevance, and context grounding.
- **Part V – Enhancement:** Cross-encoder re-ranking and HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) applied to Config A to improve retrieval quality.

## Use of AI Tools

Throughout this project, generative AI tools were used to support several parts of the workflow.

AI was used for debugging Python code, resolving library-specific questions (LangChain, ChromaDB, FAISS, NetworkX), advising on architectural decisions such as the RAG pipeline design and graph integration strategy, and reviewing pull requests. AI also supported the writing of explanatory text throughout the notebook to ensure clarity and grammatical correctness, as this report is written in English as a non-native language.

AI was also used during active coding sessions to accelerate boilerplate code generation, particularly for the RAG chain setup, graph-lookup functions, and evaluation scoring logic.

It is important to note that AI tools occasionally produced ambiguous or inconsistent answers, particularly for complex pipeline logic or edge cases in library APIs. All outputs were critically reviewed, and final decisions - including graph integration strategy, retrieval design choices, and evaluation interpretations - were made manually by the team.
